statement: Global data-centre electricity use in 2027 is below the IEA's 2025 base-case projection for 2027 (IEA; 2028 release)
status_at_phase_end: 2025 is the year the reference projection was published (IEA 'Energy and AI', 2025-04-10): 415 TWh in 2024 -> ~945 TWh in 2030 (Base Case, ~15%/yr); the implied 2027 value is ~664 TWh (third-party sum of chart components; IEA gives no headline 2027 number). Sensitivity cases bracket 2030 at ~670 TWh (Headwinds) to >1,260 TWh (Lift-Off); the Headwinds path is the closest analogue to YES. Later 2025 IEA publications (mid-year electricity update, World Energy Outlook in November) reiterated strong data-centre-led demand and grid bottleneck risk (~20% of planned projects at risk of delay). No actual 2025 consumption figure was published in-phase.

items.summary: The reference projection: the IEA's first special report on energy and AI estimates data-centre electricity at ~415 TWh in 2024 (~1.5% of global use, +12%/yr since 2017) and projects ~945 TWh by 2030 in its Base Case (~15%/yr), ~1,200 TWh by 2035. Bloc A ~45% and Bloc B ~25% of 2024 consumption.
items.detail: IEA 'Energy and AI' (2025-04-10), executive summary and 'Energy demand from AI' chapter. Bloc A +240 TWh (+130%), Bloc B +175 TWh (+170%) to 2030. Implied 2027 Base Case ~664 TWh is a third-party derivation (BinaryBriefing) from IEA chart components; confirm against the IEA data explorer before resolution.

items.summary: Same report's sensitivity cases: Headwinds (slower AI adoption, local bottlenecks, tight supply chain) ~670 TWh in 2030 and a plateau ~700 TWh; High Efficiency ~800 TWh (2030); Lift-Off >1,260 TWh (2030) and >1,700 TWh (2035). A 2027 outcome below the Base Case would resemble the Headwinds or High Efficiency paths.
items.detail: IEA 'Energy and AI' sensitivity-case section; 2030 case values per Latitude Media and Silicon & Systems summaries of the report. Range 700-1,700 TWh in 2035.

items.summary: The report flags supply-side bottlenecks: ~20% of planned data-centre projects could be delayed by grid constraints; transformer and cable wait times doubled in three years; gas-turbine lead times of several years.
items.detail: IEA 'Energy and AI' executive summary (PDF). The bottleneck mechanism is the main route by which actual 2027 use could undershoot the Base Case.
items.value: ~20% of planned projects at risk of delay

items.summary: IEA's technology director warned that an escalating tariff war could slow data-centre growth, with the two leading jurisdictions and one other bloc set to account for most growth by 2030.
items.detail: Reuters 2025-04-10, interview with Laura Cozzi (IEA). Snippet-level verification only.

items.summary: IEA mid-year electricity update: Bloc A demand growth accelerating in 2025-2026 (2.3% and 2.2%/yr), driven mainly by data-centre expansion; big-tech 2025 capex commitments of ~$320B vs $230B in 2024. Bloc B services-sector demand +7.1% in H1 2025 partly on data centres.
items.detail: IEA 'Electricity Mid-Year Update 2025', demand chapter (July 2025; exact day not verified). Bloc A data centres ~180 TWh in 2024.

items.summary: IEA's annual outlook: data-centre investment expected to reach ~$580B in 2025 (more than global oil-supply investment); data-centre electricity to triple by 2035; >85% of new capacity in the two leading jurisdictions and one other bloc; grid spending lagging generation, raising congestion.
items.detail: IEA World Energy Outlook 2025 executive summary (released 2025-11-12; Data Center Knowledge 2025-11-13). Box 8.1 updates Bloc A supply outlook for policy changes. No revised 2027 data-centre number found.

items.summary: No measured 2025 global data-centre electricity figure was published within the phase; the reference projection publishes 2024 and 2030 headline values only, so the 2027 threshold is derived.
items.detail: First IEA actual for 2025 (485 TWh) appeared 2026-04-16, outside this phase.
